items.fight_news: Moving up to welterweight changes the power dynamics; McGregor's reliance on his southpaw straight left will test Holloway's historically granite chin early in the fight.

If the bout extends into the championship rounds, Holloway's high-volume, pressure-boxing approach is perfectly designed to exploit McGregor's tendency to fatigue when forced to fight off his back foot.

bouts.title: Benoît Saint Denis vs. Paddy Pimblett

items.fight_news: Saint Denis possesses suffocating judo and chain-wrestling against the fence, which directly counters Pimblett's reliance on chaotic, open-space scrambles.
Pimblett has a severe tendency to leave his chin exposed on entries; Saint Denis must utilize intercepting knees or check hooks to punish the Englishman's aggressive forward movement.
Sandhagen's elite switch-stance footwork and flying knees will be vital to keeping Bautista's relentless wrestling pressure at bay.
Bautista must avoid striking at range and instead time Sandhagen's spinning attacks to secure body locks and drain the striker's energy on the mat.
Royval thrives in pure chaos, using unorthodox submission attempts to confuse strikers. Kavanagh must maintain pristine kickboxing fundamentals and refuse to engage in ground scrambles.
If Kavanagh can keep the fight strictly in striking range, his technical precision gives him a massive statistical edge over Royval's wild, looping entries.
McKinney is notoriously explosive in the first round but fades rapidly. Green's hands-down, shoulder-roll defense relies entirely on reflexes to survive this terrifying initial three-minute window.
If Green survives the first round, his economical jab and high-volume output will easily overwhelm a fatigued McKinney.
Moving up to light heavyweight, Whittaker will enjoy a massive speed advantage but must navigate Krylov's long kicks and heavy top control.
The blitzing jab-cross combination is Whittaker's best weapon to close the distance against the much larger Russian veteran.
Steveson's Olympic gold-medal wrestling pedigree means he will absolutely dictate where this fight takes place.
Ellison's only realistic path to victory relies on a perfectly timed uppercut or knee during Steveson's inevitable level changes.
Garbrandt's hand speed remains elite, but his defensive liability in the pocket plays perfectly into Yanez's sharp, counter-boxing combinations.
Yanez's check left hook is the most critical metric of the fight; he must catch Garbrandt stepping in recklessly.

bouts.title: Luke Riley vs. Kai Kamaka III

items.fight_news: Riley relies on precise, technical striking from the outside. Kamaka brings a grinding, wrestling-heavy approach specifically designed to put Riley on his back.
Cortez heavily relies on cage control and grinding takedowns. Cong's elite Sanda background gives her a massive advantage in open-space kickboxing.
Cong must utilize lateral footwork and stiff teep kicks to stop Cortez from initiating the clinch.
Almeida's high-level kickboxing pedigree means Pinas must secure takedowns to win. Pinas has a reach advantage but must use it strictly to mask his shots, not to trade strikes.
Basharat executes seamless striking-to-grappling transitions. Garza must focus entirely on framing and escaping off the fence, as Basharat's top control is suffocating.
Reese possesses a massive height and reach advantage, requiring Gandra to slip inside and attack the body.
If Gandra's footwork remains linear, Reese's long kicks will easily keep him at bay for all three rounds.
Durden relies on relentless chain wrestling, which directly clashes with Costa's explosive boxing and heavy low kicks.
Costa must rely heavily on his check hook to punish Durden's aggressive takedown attempts and keep the fight standing.
